title: GST return section specification
description: Meta-schema for per-section spec files (spec/gstr1/*.json, spec/gstr3b/*.json). A section spec describes one table of a return: where its rows come from (Excel sheet / CSV), what each column means and must satisfy, cross-field rules, how rows group into records, and how records map onto the portal upload payload.

$schema.description: Relative path back to this meta-schema, so editors validate section specs as they are written.

section.description: Section code as used by the official tooling (b2b, b2ba, cdnr, ...). Unique within a return.

title.description: Human-readable section name, including the statutory table numbers it feeds.

provenance.description: Which official artifact versions this spec was derived from. Lets a spec file be re-verified against a pinned release.

verified_on.description: ISO date the spec was last checked against the artifacts above.

source.description: Where rows are read from. A section may be importable from an Excel sheet, a section CSV, or both.

sheet.description: Worksheet name, matched exactly (names contain commas, e.g. 'b2b,sez,de').

first_data_row.description: 1-based row of the first data record. Error messages report this offset, so a 0-based record index i maps to sheet row i + first_data_row.

max_data_row.description: Last row the official template's data validation covers, where one exists. Rows beyond it are outside the template's guarantees.

file.description: Filename in the official section-wise CSV set.

fields.description: Column definitions in template order. `order` is the 0-based column position; both Excel and CSV use the same order unless a field overrides it.

rules.description: Cross-field rules, evaluated per row after field-level validation passes. Each is a `when` predicate (omitted = always) implying an `assert` predicate.

grouping.description: How validated rows collapse into records. Sections are row-per-tax-rate: several rows sharing an invoice key become one invoice with several line items.

envelope_key.description: Field ids that group invoices into an outer payload object (e.g. one object per recipient GSTIN). Absent for flat sections.

invoice_key.description: Field ids identifying one invoice/document within an envelope.

invoice_key_case_insensitive.description: Whether invoice-key comparison folds case. The official tool lowercases document numbers before matching.

item_key.description: Field ids identifying one line item within an invoice. Absent for sections with no item level.

item_conflict.description: What happens when two rows share both an invoice key and an item key. `last_wins`: the later row silently replaces the earlier one (no summing, no error).

invoice_field_conflict.description: What happens when rows sharing an invoice key disagree on an invoice-level field. `error`: the whole invoice is rejected.

output.description: Mapping onto the portal upload payload.

derivations.description: Named computations the engine implements, referenced by payload keys whose value is computed rather than mapped. Documented in `derivation_notes`.

derivation_notes.description: Prose + formula for each derivation named above, keyed by derivation name.

notes.description: Free-form observations: quirks of the reference behavior, open questions, deliberate divergences.

id.description: Stable internal identifier, matching the portal payload key where one exists.

column.description: Column header text, matched exactly after trimming.

type.description: Value domain, independent of which values are allowed — restrict those with `enum` or `enum_ref`. `decimal` values are exact (never binary floating point) and are emitted as JSON numbers; `text` is emitted as a string. `state_code` is a 'NN-Name' cell reduced to its numeric prefix.

required.description: Whether the cell must be non-empty. A field with a `default` is satisfied when empty, by taking that default.

default.description: Value substituted when the cell is empty, before validation.

pattern.description: Regular expression the raw cell text must match.

accepts.description: For `gstin` fields: which registration-number forms are accepted, most-specific first.

enum_ref.description: Pointer to a masters file supplying the allowed values, as 'file#/json/pointer'.

enum.description: Inline allowed values, when too small or too section-specific for a masters file.

constraints.description: Named field-level checks beyond pattern/enum, implemented by the engine.

transform.description: Named normalization applied to the accepted value before grouping and output.

must_be_empty.description: The column exists in the template but no value is permitted for this section.

id.description: Stable rule identifier, namespaced by section (e.g. 'b2b.cbw_requires_rchrg'). Referenced by error reports and tests.

when.description: Guard predicate. Omitted means the assertion always applies.

assert.description: Predicate that must hold when the guard does.

message.description: Operator-facing message, phrased in template vocabulary (column headers, not field ids).

predicate.description: Boolean expression over a row's fields. Exactly one form per object: a leaf comparison on a single field, or a combinator over sub-predicates. Deliberately not an expression language — the engine walks this structure directly.

field.description: Field id under test. Required for leaf forms.

ne.description: Field does not equal this value.

in.description: Field is one of these values.

empty.description: true: field is absent or blank. false: field has a value.

payload_object.description: One level of the upload JSON. Keys are payload key names; values say where the content comes from.

key.description: Key name in the upload JSON.

from.description: `field:<id>` maps a field; `derive:<name>` computes it; `nested:<level>` embeds the level below.

omit_when_empty.description: Key is left out entirely rather than emitted as null or empty string.

verify.description: Marks a key whose presence or exact form is not yet confirmed. `oracle`: must be settled by differential capture against the official tool before this section is trusted.

kind.description: `quirk`: reference behavior that is surprising but reproduced deliberately. `open_question`: unresolved, needs oracle capture. `divergence`: where this implementation intentionally differs.

affects.description: Field ids, rule ids, or payload keys this note concerns.
